data.headline: S&P futures shorts shrink as asset-manager net longs fall
data.summary: In the week to November 10, leveraged funds cut their E-mini S&P 500 net short by 69,258 contracts while the asset-manager net long fell by 14,454. Total open interest rose.

bull.text: The leveraged-fund net short fell from 372,318 to 303,060 contracts between November 3 and 10, reflecting both higher long holdings and lower short holdings.

bear.text: The asset-manager net long fell from 928,584 to 914,130 contracts. Short holdings rose by more than long holdings in the same report.

watch.text: Open interest rose from 1,986,532 to 2,017,687 contracts. Check the next weekly report for whether both positioning changes persist as the number of open contracts changes.
The two-year Treasury yield eased to 4.83% on November 16 from 4.88% on November 13. It remained 27 basis points above November 9, a useful benchmark for tracking refinancing conditions.

limitations: The E-mini S&P 500 futures are related to SPY, but their CFTC positions measure futures activity. They do not establish SPY fund flows or investor intent.
The November 10 position report and November 16 yield have different observation dates. This report has no verified SPY closing price, return, options exposure or dealer gamma.
